title: Alto saxophone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS alto saxophone (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: Stand-in saxophone, not a measured one. No tone holes: each note is the printed mouthpiece, neck and bell cones joined by one straight cone cut to that note's length, where a real saxophone plays these notes with holes. The reed's opening, width and area are borrowed. C4 is blown at mf, E3 and F3 at ff, because they were silent at mf on this reed before the closure stop (not tried again since). One mouthpiece position, pushed in 13.28 mm and solved once on C4's passive peak, leaves the three at +26.4, -10.6 and -7.7 c from equal temperament. All three are cleaner than the recordings, and C4's seventh harmonic sits 9 dB under its sixth. All three pages are re-renders after the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17); on the old law the reed passed through its lay on 17 to 19 % of steady samples. Ab4 and E5 stay empty: with a register hole borrowed from a soprano they play an octave low.
physics_present: The printed neck (ISMA 2007), bell and mouthpiece (Lefebvre 2010) joined by one straight body cone whose slope is set once from the lowest note, Db3, and cut to each note's length
An alto reed fitted to a Lefebvre mouthpiece (his printed mass per area, resonance and damping); its opening 1.7 mm, width 10 mm and area 7.5e-5 m2 are borrowed
One mouthpiece position for every note, pushed in 13.28 mm, solved once on C4's passive first peak against equal temperament
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two alto players
Reed noise, the duct-constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990), extrapolated, with no level set against a recording
A flanged bell radiating into room air with ISO 9613 absorption, 0.5 m on axis, at 48 kHz because the engine refuses this bell at 96 kHz
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)
physics_missing: Tone holes, pads, chimneys, key rise and a fingering chart: no measured alto air column is printed, so no hole lattice is built
A measured alto reed opening, width and area: the opening is an unplayed-tip upper bound, the width a tenor reed's and the area Lefebvre's illustrative value
The right pitch: the three sit +26.4, -10.6 and -7.7 c from equal temperament, a 37 c spread; whether one position can close it was read on the old law only
The recordings' spectra and noise: harmonics-to-noise reads 1 to 5 dB above the recordings on all three notes, and C4's centroid is 1180 Hz against 405 Hz
The second register: with a register hole borrowed from a soprano, placed by Scavone's rule, Ab4 and E5 sound an octave low, so they stay empty
